novi-sad-station-canopy-collapse.conditions_add: The China Eximbank preferential buyer credit loan agreement of 25 April 2019 for the Novi Sad-Subotica-state border (Kelebija) railway section, a loan of up to US$988,388,500 to the Government of Serbia represented by the Ministry of Finance against the commercial contract of 7 July 2018 with the joint venture of China Railway International Co. Ltd and China Communications Construction Company Ltd, required that goods, technologies and services bought with the money "shall be purchased from China preferentially according to the Commercial Contract" (Article 2.5). Article 2.4 limited the money to "the sole purpose of the payment of approximately eighty five percent (85%) of the Commercial Contract amount" and barred its use for "brokerage fees, agency fees or commission". Before each drawdown the Serbian side had to show documents proving it had paid the contractor without using loan money, so that the ratio of its own funds to the loan "shall not be lower than 15:85" (Appendix 1).

plan-colombia-aerial-spraying.conditions_add: Congress attached conditions to this money in the FY2002 foreign operations appropriations act, P.L. 107-115, enacted in January 2002; a Congressional Research Service brief records that the act "included conditions on the use of funds for purchase of chemicals for the aerial spraying program in Colombia". Under the act's Andean Counterdrug Initiative heading, funds used for the procurement of chemicals for aerial coca fumigation could be made available only if the Secretary of State, after consulting the Environmental Protection Agency, the Department of Agriculture and, if appropriate, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, determined and reported to the appropriations committees that the fumigation was being carried out in accordance with EPA regulatory controls "as labeled for use in the United States", that the chemicals as applied "do not pose unreasonable risks or adverse effects to humans or the environment", and that "procedures are available to evaluate claims of local citizens that their health was harmed or their licit agricultural crops were damaged" and to pay fair compensation for meritorious claims. The same act barred the money for spraying after six months from enactment unless alternative development programmes had been developed "in consultation with communities and local authorities" in the departments where spraying was planned or had taken place (P.L. 107-115, 115 Stat. 2130-2131).

why.safeguard: do not pose unreasonable risks or adverse effects to humans or the environment
why.admin: procedures are available to evaluate claims of local citizens that their health was harmed or their licit agricultural crops were damaged

sources_add.title: Public Law 107-115, Foreign Operations, Export Financing, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2002 (Andean Counterdrug Initiative heading, 115 Stat. 2130-2131)
Drug Control: International Policy and Approaches (Issue Brief IB88093)

plan-colombia-aerial-spraying.searched: Fact-check round. The Congressional Research Service brief does confirm that P.L. 107-115 carried conditions on the chemicals money, so the statutory route is sound, but the tests quoted in the previous draft came from the State Department's December 2003 Memorandum of Justification, which cites the FY2003 act (P.L. 108-7) and never mentions P.L. 107-115, and the previous draft's 20 percent cap appears only in that later act. The conditions above are therefore taken from the enacted text of P.L. 107-115 itself on govinfo (Andean Counterdrug Initiative heading, 115 Stat. 2130-2131), which falls inside the 2000-2015 spraying period on this card. The 2003 Memorandum of Justification has been dropped as a source for this entry.
